content:
America’s Hybrid Hype Has Hit the Used Market

Demand for hybrid vehicles is so high that some used cars are selling for more than new ones. The surge in interest has driven prices in the secondary market above the cost of newly manufactured models. This trend highlights the growing popularity of hybrids among American consumers.
summary: Demand for hybrid cars in the U.S. used market is extremely high. Some used hybrids are selling for more than new ones.
author: Wired

title: Best Battery-Powered Leaf Blowers 2026 Tested for Power, Battery Life, and Noise
content:
Best Battery-Powered Leaf Blowers (2026): Tested for Power, Battery Life, and Noise

A recent review highlights the shift from gas to cordless leaf blowers, emphasizing their performance, battery endurance, and noise levels. The tester evaluated several battery-powered models on a variety of surfaces.

The blowers were put to the test on gravel, wood chips, and even a 5‑pound concrete paver, demonstrating their capability across different terrains.
summary: I tested these cordless leaf blowers on gravel, wood chips, and a 5-pound concrete paver. The test evaluated power, battery life, and noise.
author: Wired

title: Dunking on Dating App Profiles Becomes Viral Content, Users Annoyed
content:
Dunking on dating app profiles has become a popular content trend, but many users are growing tired of it. The trend, highlighted in the title, draws attention to the growing frustration with how profiles are presented online.

Relationship coaches, TikTokers, and disgruntled singles alike frequently shame bad profiles. Their critiques often focus on poorly curated photos, vague bios, and other perceived shortcomings that can deter potential matches.

In response, more dating apps are experimenting with blocking screenshots, a move that could limit the ability of users to share or highlight others’ profiles in the same way.
summary: Relationship coaches, TikTokers, and disgruntled singles frequently shame bad dating app profiles. More apps are experimenting with blocking screenshots.
author: Wired

title: Microsoft 365 Family Subscribers to Share AI Benefits with Plan Members
content:
Microsoft has announced that it will expand the use of its AI‑powered Office features to all members of a Microsoft 365 Family or Premium subscription.  

The change follows last year’s rollout of AI‑powered Office tools, which had been limited to the primary account holder.  The new update will allow the primary user to share Copilot and other AI usage benefits, as well as access to Office apps and OneDrive storage, with up to five additional people on the same plan.  

The company detailed the upcoming adjustments in an email sent to Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers, noting that the changes will take effect over the coming months.  The full story is available on The Verge.
summary: Microsoft is enabling Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers to share Copilot and AI usage features with up to five other people on the plan. The change also allows shared access to Office apps and OneDrive storage, announced in an email to subscribers with updates coming over the next months.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI defends firing of three AI safety researchers over breach of trust
content:
OpenAI has reaffirmed its decision to fire three safety researchers after an investigation found a significant breach of trust.

The researchers—Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni—were dismissed for violating “clear policies on handling sensitive information,” according to a post on X released on Friday.

OpenAI said the firings were not related to the trio’s public comments or concerns about AI safety. The post was a direct response to an open letter the researchers published on Thursday urging the company to be more transparent about the decision.
summary: OpenAI said it dismissed Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni for violating clear policies on handling sensitive information after an investigation found a significant breach of trust. The company stated the firings were not related to the researchers' public concerns about AI safety and posted the response on X following their open letter demanding transparency.
author: The Verge

title: Playdate handheld hailed as top gaming deal as season 3 adds eight games
content:
The Playdate, Panic’s tiny yellow handheld that launched in 2022, has become one of gaming’s best deals.  

Despite its unconventional design—a black‑and‑white screen and a crank jutting from the side—the device has built a strong and constantly growing library of games.  

For its newest offering, Playdate’s season 3, the company is releasing eight games as part of a curated “season” collection, with two titles launching each week.  

The ongoing seasonal releases continue to improve the handheld’s value proposition.
summary: Panic's tiny yellow Playdate handheld, launched in 2022 with a black‑and‑white screen and a side crank, has built a strong and growing library of games. Season 3 introduces eight new games released two per week, further cementing the device as one of gaming’s best‑value deals.
author: The Verge

title: Meta bans ByteDance TikTok ads in US and other countries
content:
Meta has prohibited advertisements from TikTok’s Chinese parent company ByteDance on its platforms in the United States and several other countries. The ban, which took effect on Thursday, blocks both direct ads and paid marketing messages from ByteDance as well as third‑party ads that link to TikTok.

Meta spokesperson Christopher Sgro told The Verge that the company “doesn’t have to run ads from a competitor whose goal is to pull people off our apps,” adding that declining promotional services to a competitor is “a normal business practice across industries.” The move comes as competition between the two major social‑media operators intensifies.
summary: Meta has banned ads from TikTok's Chinese parent ByteDance on its platforms in the United States and several other countries. The Thursday‑effective ban blocks ByteDance ads and third‑party ads that link to TikTok, according to a statement by Meta spokesperson Christopher Sgro.
author: The Verge

title: Falcon 9 scrub occurs as officials say Vulcan launch is weeks away
content: A recent rocket report noted a rare Falcon 9 scrub and questioned whether the setback signals an opportunity for United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket. The piece referenced a statement that “I can say we’re weeks away from launching on Vulcan.” No additional information about the scrub or the launch schedule was provided.
summary: A rare Falcon 9 scrub was reported. A source said they are weeks away from launching on Vulcan.
author: Ars Technica

title: Xona's navigation service to enter beta after SpaceX launches six satellites
content:
Xona’s commercial GPS alternative is poised to go live as its precision timing and navigation service moves into beta testing. The upcoming testing phase follows the launch of six satellites that were designed by the company.

SpaceX will carry out the launch of the six Xona‑designed satellites, after which Xona plans to begin beta trials of its service.
summary: Xona's precision timing and navigation service will enter beta testing. The beta phase will begin after SpaceX launches six satellites designed by Xona.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says world must accept some AI harms
content:
Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, told Politico’s technology podcast and newsletter Decoded that the world must tolerate “some bad things” in order to reap the benefits of artificial‑intelligence technology and preserve users’ agency. “One of the differences between us and some of the stricter AI safety people is that we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency [to use it],” Altman said.

The commentary notes that AI has already been implicated in violent deaths and “nearly started world war three,” suggesting that such harmful outcomes tend to affect others rather than the developers themselves. The piece is authored by Moustafa Bayoumi, an award‑winning writer, professor of English at Brooklyn College, City University of New York, and a Guardian US columnist.
summary: Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, told Politico’s Decoded podcast and newsletter that the world should accept some bad things happening from artificial intelligence for its benefits and user agency. The article says AI has already been implicated in violent deaths and nearly started world war three.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic bans users for sustained abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude
content:
Anthropic announced that it will bar users who engage in “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior” toward its AI models, including the Claude chatbot.  

A company spokesperson said the specific definition of abusive or cruel content has not yet been provided. The policy change was first reported by The Verge.  

The ban comes as Anthropic’s leaders continue to contemplate questions of machine consciousness.
summary: Anthropic has not yet specified what counts as abusive or cruel content. The company barred users from exhibiting sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward its models, a policy change reported by The Verge.
author: Guardian Technology

title: OpenAI cuts projected 2024 revenue to $50bn, $20bn below prior estimate
content:
OpenAI has told investors that its revenue for the current year is expected to reach $50 billion (£37 billion), based on sales through the end of September. This forecast is about $20 billion lower than the $70 billion figure the company had previously signaled to investors.

The revision has prompted questions about the pace of growth in demand for artificial‑intelligence products, including the company’s ChatGPT service. OpenAI’s updated projection reflects a significant shortfall from earlier expectations.
summary: OpenAI told investors its revenue for this year will be $50bn, about $20bn less than it previously indicated. The lower forecast has prompted questions about the rapid growth rate in demand for AI.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Palantir senior VP Tom Watson warns against “mob rule” in government contract awards
content:
Former Labour deputy leader Tom Watson, who has recently joined Palantir as a senior vice‑president, warned that “mob rule” should not dictate the awarding of public contracts. In a statement, Watson cautioned that UK ministers could “get themselves in a lot of trouble” if they allow the government to work with his new employer on immigration crackdowns.

Watson was questioned about concerns that the Palantir‑Reform UK partnership could influence government policy. He reiterated that the tech firm would work with a Reform UK government on immigration crackdowns, but stressed that public contracts must be awarded fairly and not be subject to populist pressure.

The remarks come as Watson has moved from a political career to a corporate role, highlighting the potential conflicts between his former public duties and his new position at Palantir.
summary: Tom Watson, former Labour deputy leader and senior vice‑president at Palantir, said “mob rule” must not dictate awarding of public contracts. He warned UK ministers could get “in a lot of trouble” over concerns about government work with his new employer and said the firm could work with a Reform UK government on immigration crackdowns.
author: Guardian Technology

title: East Fishkill, NY faces backlash over new AI datacenter in former IBM town
content:
A fight in East Fishkill, New York, has become part of a growing divide over whether the benefits of artificial intelligence outweigh its enormous downsides, with local residents voicing backlash to a proposed datacenter in the hamlet.

East Fishkill, located 70 miles north of New York City, helped build New York’s tech industry. The hamlet was home to a 460‑acre campus where IBM researched and manufactured semiconductor chips for nearly fifty years.
summary: A dispute has erupted in East Fishkill, New York, over an AI datacenter, reflecting a broader debate about AI’s benefits and downsides. The hamlet, located 70 miles north of New York City, previously hosted IBM’s 460‑acre semiconductor research and manufacturing campus for nearly fifty years.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Jeremy Strong’s Mark Zuckerberg role in ‘The Social Reckoning’ reflects shifting view of tech CEOs
content:
Jeremy Strong’s portrayal of Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Reckoning illustrates how public opinion has shifted around billionaire CEOs since The Social Network premiered. The film’s depiction highlights the changing perception of tech leaders in contemporary culture.

When The Social Network was released, Mark Zuckerberg organized a staff viewing of the movie, describing it as “fun.” This corporate outing reflected the initial, more light‑hearted view of tech executives at the time.

According to the article, a group corporate outing to the sequel is unlikely, underscoring the evolving relationship between tech leaders and their public image.
summary: Jeremy Strong portrays Mark Zuckerberg in the film The Social Reckoning, showing how public opinion of billionaire CEOs has changed since The Social Network’s release. When The Social Network premiered, Zuckerberg organized a staff viewing of a film he called “fun,” but a corporate outing to the sequel is unlikely.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meredith Whittaker warns careless AI use is real threat in BBC Global Women interview
content:
Meredith Whittaker said in an exclusive interview with BBC Global Women that artificial‑intelligence technology has been misunderstood. She argues that the real danger lies in careless use of AI, rather than the more sensational ghost‑story narratives that sometimes dominate public discussion.  

Whittaker’s remarks were made during the interview, which focused on the need for clearer understanding and responsible deployment of AI technologies.
summary: Meredith Whittaker says careless use of AI is the real threat, not ghost stories. She said this in an exclusive interview with BBC Global Women.
author: BBC Technology

title: Cars burned, shops looted in anti-immigration protests in Soweto and Durban
content:
Cars were set ablaze and shops were looted during violent anti‑immigration protests in South Africa on Thursday, 8 October. The unrest unfolded in the townships of Soweto and the city of Durban.

Protesters took to the streets after a Constitutional Court ruling that eased restrictions on asylum applications, prompting the destructive demonstrations. No further details on casualties or arrests were provided.
summary: Violent anti‑immigration protests in Soweto and Durban saw cars burned and shops looted. The unrest on Thursday, 8 October followed a Constitutional Court ruling that eased restrictions on asylum applications.
author: Euronews

title: Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores wins Queropalca vote by 25 votes
content:
Left‑wing candidate Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores won a local election in Queropalca, a district of just over 730 residents in Peru’s Huánuco department. He secured the victory by a margin of 25 votes while running for the centre‑left Ahora Nación party.

The result marks another instance of a candidate named Hitler being elected in Peru; he is not the country’s first elected Hitler.
summary: Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores, running for the centre-left Ahora Nación party, won the local election in Queropalca, a district of just over 730 people in the Huánuco department, by 25 votes. He is not Peru’s first elected Hitler.
author: Euronews

title: Houthi missile strikes hit Riyadh's King Khalid Airport, killing three including a captain
content:
Houthi missile strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed three people, including an airline captain, according to the headline.  

Two missiles hit the airport, forcing diplomats to shelter in place and causing delays to dozens of flights.  

Yemen’s government said it was making progress in its Red Sea counter‑offensive, while Houthi forces said they were holding their ground.
summary: Two missile strikes hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, killing three people, among them an airline captain. The attacks forced diplomats to shelter in place and delayed dozens of flights, while Yemen’s government said its Red Sea counter‑offensive was making progress and Houthi forces said they were holding their ground.
author: Euronews

title: Putin says Russia will help end US‑Iran war after meeting Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan
content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said he would help end the war between the United States and Iran, even as Russia maintains its own conflict in Ukraine.  

During a meeting in Turkmenistan with Iranian official Pezeshkian, Putin pledged to do “everything in our power” to bring an end to the US‑Iran war. He noted that Russia is not listed among the official mediators of the dispute.
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan. He pledged to do “everything in our power” to end the war between the United States and Iran, noting Russia is not an official mediator.
author: Euronews

title: Tens of thousands march in Madrid to mourn evicted pensioner Maricarmen Abascal
content:
Tens of thousands of people gathered in Madrid to mourn pensioner Maricarmen Abascal, whose recent eviction has turned her into a symbol of the city’s housing crisis.  

The large demonstration highlighted public anger over the eviction, which has sparked fresh protests across the capital.
summary: Tens of thousands marched in Madrid to mourn pensioner Maricarmen Abascal. Her eviction made her a housing crisis symbol and sparked fresh protests.
author: Euronews

title: Baby orangutan Novita rescued from Borneo wildfires in Central Kalimantan
content:
A three- to four‑year‑old female orangutan named Novita was rescued after a wildfire swept through Central Kalimantan, Borneo. She was found clinging to a tree on 26 September, having crossed the flames.

Novita sustained burns to her hands and feet, but survived the incident. The rescue highlights the growing threat of habitat destruction in the region.
summary: A three- to four-year-old female orangutan named Novita was rescued after being found clinging to a tree in Central Kalimantan on 26 September. She had burns on her hands and feet after crossing the flames.
author: Euronews

title: Ethiopia, Eritrea blame each other for war as rebels retreat; 8,000 Eritrean troops in Tigray
content:
Ethiopia and Eritrea each accused the other on Friday of starting a “war of agresson,” days after the two nations severed diplomatic ties.  

Ethiopian officals estimate that up to 8,000 Eritrean soldiers are operating in Tigray, supporting rebels who launched attacks against federal forces last month. The rebels are now retreating, according to the report.
summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea accused each other of starting a "war of agresson" days after severing diplomatic ties. Ethiopian officials estimate up to 8,000 Eritrean soldiers are in Tigray supporting rebels who launched attacks against federal forces last month.
author: France 24

title: Kramatorsk residents forced to flee amid intensifying Russian drone attacks
content:
Residents of Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine are increasingly forced to leave their homes as Russian drone strikes and shelling intensify. The city has come under regular attack, making the threat from drones and artillery a daily reality for those who remain.

Although many residents initially resisted evacuation, the growing danger has prompted a rising number of people to flee. Journalists from France 2 documented an evacuation from the city and reported first‑hand on the hazards faced by the population.
summary: Kramatorsk in eastern Ukraine is facing increasingly frequent Russian drone and shelling attacks, making daily life hazardous for those who remain. As the danger grows, more residents are being forced to evacuate, a process observed by France 2 reporters.
author: France 24

title: Two Renoir paintings recovered, six arrested after French Riviera museum theft
content:
Two Renoir paintings valued at millions of dollars that were stolen from a museum on the French Riviera a month ago have been recovered, and six suspects have been arrested, the local mayor said on Friday.

According to the mayor, the thieves sliced through a fence and climbed through a window before initially taking four paintings by the French master. As they fled, they abandoned two of the artworks, which were later recovered.

The recovery follows the arrest of six individuals suspected of involvement in the theft, bringing the investigation to a close.
summary: Two Renoir paintings worth millions stolen from a French Riviera museum a month ago have been recovered and six suspects arrested, the local mayor said on Friday. The thieves sliced through a fence, climbed through a window and initially stole four paintings, abandoning two as they fled.
author: France 24

title: India records 5,737 dowry-linked deaths in 2024, averaging 16 women daily
content:
India recorded 5,737 dowry‑linked deaths in 2024, an average of roughly 16 women per day, according to official figures.  

Although the transfer of money or valuables from a bride’s family at marriage has been outlawed for more than six decades, the practice remains deeply entrenched across Indian society, as reported by correspondents.
summary: India recorded 5,737 dowry-linked deaths in 2024, about 16 women per day. The practice of dowry, outlawed more than six decades ago, remains deeply entrenched across Indian society.
author: France 24

title: Aid to Africa drops over 25%, hitting women and children
content:
Foreign aid to Africa has dropped by more than 25%, prompting concerns about the impact on women and children across the continent. In Kenya, cuts to U.S.-aid‑backed health programmes for women are already being felt on the ground, according to a report from the region.

Reporter Annette Young interviewed Nana Zulu of the African Women’s Development Fund, who described how the reduction in funding threatens health services for women and could have broader repercussions for the region.

The article also highlighted the bravery of female firefighters in Borneo, who are battling Indonesia’s worst fire season in 11 years while confronting a sexist backlash against their work.
summary: International aid to Africa is shrinking, with US‑aid health programmes for women cut, impacting women and children in Kenya. The report also highlights female firefighters in Borneo confronting a sexist backlash as Indonesia experiences its worst fire season in 11 years.
author: France 24

title: French army did not deploy tanks at protests; video showed vehicle returning to base
content:
Misinformation has spread online about recent student protests in France, falsely suggesting that the French army deployed an armoured vehicle against demonstrators. A viral TikTok claimed the vehicle was used to confront protesters, but the footage actually shows the vehicle returning to a nearby military base.

Other posts have repurposed video from 2023 retirement protests as if it were current, and an AI‑generated image has been misrepresented as a police officer being attacked. Analyst Vedika Bahl notes that old, out‑of‑context and AI‑generated content are fueling the false narratives surrounding the protests.
summary: A viral TikTok claimed the French army deployed an armoured vehicle against student protesters, but the footage actually showed the vehicle returning to a nearby base. Other online posts reused 2023 protest footage and an AI‑generated image, spreading further misinformation.
author: France 24

title: Finland faces growing debt burden as war in Ukraine adds fiscal strain
content:
Finland, long celebrated as the world's happiest country, is confronting a growing debt problem that is no longer a distant concern. The nation’s fiscal health has deteriorated, and the debt pile is now a source of unease for many Finns.

The conflict in Ukraine has further strained Finland’s finances, adding to the country’s fiscal burden. The war’s economic impact has compounded existing debt pressures, making the situation more urgent.

Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them.
summary: Finland, often called the world's happiest country, is confronting a debt problem that can no longer be ignored. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden, prompting questions about whether the nation can absorb another shock.
author: DW World

title: Bosnia to elect new Grand Mufti on Oct. 10
content:
Bosnia and Herzegovina will soon have a new Grand Mufti.  
The Islamic Community in the country is set to elect its new reis‑ul‑ulema on October 10.  

The position of Grand Mufti is important for Muslims in Bosnia and Herzegovina and, according to the community, could serve as an inspiration for Muslims across Europe.
summary: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema’s role is important for Muslims in the country and could inspire Muslims across Europe.
author: DW World

title: India's 'cockroaches' vs Election Commission: What you need to know ahead of CJP's October 10 protests
content:
New Delhi has been transformed into a fortress, with train and metro services cancelled, barricades erected and a heavy police presence deployed. The measures come in preparation for Saturday’s planned protests against the chief of India’s electoral body.  

The demonstrations are set for October 10, targeting the chief of the Election Commission.
summary: The Indian capital New Delhi has been turned into a fortress with train and metro cancelations, barricades and heavy police presence ahead of Saturday's planned protests against the chief of India's electoral body.
author: DW World

title: Ukrainian Refugee Lifeline in Poland Faces Donor Fatigue and Rising Hostility
content: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country created a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Her organization now confronts donor fatigue, funding cuts, and rising hostility. The decline in support for Ukrainians in Poland has intensified these challenges.
summary: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war created a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Her organization now struggles with donor fatigue, funding cuts, and increasing hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.
author: DW World

title: ICJ Judge Navi Pillay Awarded Nobel Peace Prize for Promoting International Law
content:
Navi Pillay, a South African judge on the International Court of Justice, has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The Norwegian Nobel Committee recognized her work as a former United Nations human‑rights chief and as chair of the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza.

The committee said Pillay “has shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence.” Her receipt of the prize highlights her contributions to promoting international law.
summary: Navi Pillay, a South African former UN human rights chief and current ICJ judge, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The Norwegian Nobel Committee praised her for showing that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence.
author: Guardian World

title: Mourinho Lashes Out at Criticism of Mbappe's Knee Injury Recovery
content:
Real Madrid manager José Mourinho has publicly condemned criticism directed at Kylian Mbappé, describing the remarks as “ridiculous.”  

Mbappé has faced scrutiny over his chosen method of recovering from a knee injury as he prepares to rejoin Real Madrid’s squad. Mourinho’s remarks came as the French forward continues his rehabilitation ahead of his return to the club.
summary: Real Madrid manager Mourinho criticized the criticism of Kylian Mbappe's recovery from a knee injury. Mbappe is preparing to return to Real Madrid after the injury.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Indian artists face censorship as New Delhi removes satirical content under new rules
content:
Indian artists are encountering increased censorship as anti‑Modi protests expand, according to reports. The government in New Delhi has been accused of silencing dissent by removing satirical content and online critiques.

The removals are being carried out under newly introduced rules that target such material.
summary: New Delhi has been accused of silencing dissent by removing satirical content and online critiques under new rules. The censorship comes as anti‑Modi protests grow, affecting Indian artists.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Malaysia closes schools due to haze from Indonesian forest fires
content: Malaysia has shut schools as haze from Indonesian forest fires spreads across Southeast Asia. Kuala Lumpur’s Air Pollutant Index reports that air quality has reached unhealthy levels amid the smog. The deteriorating conditions highlight the cross‑border impact of the fires on the region.
summary: Malaysia shut schools as haze from Indonesian forest fires spread across Southeast Asia. Kuala Lumpur's Air Pollutant Index reported unhealthy air quality amid smog from the fires.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukraine drones strike Yandex and Russian missile plants, oil refineries
content:
Ukraine has begun targeting Russia’s artificial‑intelligence data infrastructure, according to recent reports.  

Drone attacks have struck the Russian digital giant Yandex, while separate strikes have continued against missile production facilities and oil refineries.  

These operations reflect a broader Ukrainian effort to disrupt key Russian technology and industrial assets.
summary: Drone attacks have targeted Russian digital giant Yandex. Ukraine also continues strikes on missile plants and oil refineries.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Child flees as Israeli settlers hijack car during pogrom
content:
A Palestinian boy was seen fleeing after Israeli settlers attacked his father and hijacked their car in Ramallah, an incident described as part of a pogrom.  

The settlers assaulted the boy’s father before stealing the vehicle, prompting the child to run away from the scene. The event occurred in the West Bank city of Ramallah.  

The incident highlights ongoing tensions in the area.
summary: A Palestinian boy was seen fleeing after Israeli settlers attacked his father and stole their car in Ramallah.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukraine pushes Russia back in Donetsk as casualties rise
content:
Ukraine is advancing against Russian forces in the Donetsk region, prompting a retreat of Russian units from several settlements they previously controlled. The fighting has intensified as Russia struggles to hold onto areas it once firmly held.

According to the headline, both military and civilian casualties are rising sharply amid the renewed combat in Donetsk.
summary: Russia is fighting for settlements it once firmly held in Donetsk, while Ukraine pushes it back. Russia has retreated from many other settlements as military and civilian casualties are soaring.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Thieves steal 30,000 wine bottles valued at €5 million from Florence winery
content:
Thieves stole 30,000 wine bottles valued at €5 million in Italy, according to reports.  

The heist took place at a winery based in Florence and is believed to be one of the largest thefts of its kind in the country.
summary: Thieves stole 30,000 wine bottles worth €5 million from a Florence-based winery, according to reports. The theft is believed to be one of the largest of its kind in Italy.
author: BBC World

title: Ethiopia warns Eritrea of self‑defence after Eritrean troops cross border
content: Ethiopia has warned Eritrea that it will defend itself after Eritrean troops crossed the border. Truckloads of Eritrean soldiers were observed driving into Ethiopian territory, prompting a response that included drone strikes, according to reports. The Ethiopian government’s warning follows these incursions and the subsequent aerial attacks. No further details were provided.
summary: Truckloads of Eritrean soldiers have been seen driving into Ethiopia. Ethiopia has reportedly responded with drone strikes.
author: BBC World

title: France pledges 3,000 extra teachers to quell high‑school protests
content:
France announced a plan to add 3,000 teachers as an initial measure to ease ongoing student protests.  

Education minister Edouard Geffray presented the offer following another day of sometimes violent demonstrations by high‑school students. The pledge aims to address concerns raised by the unrest.
summary: Education minister Edouard Geffray announced that France will add 3,000 teachers. The offer follows another day of sometimes violent demonstrations by high‑school students.
author: BBC World

title: Fort Hood survivor backs firing‑squad execution, doubts livestream
content:
Alonzo Lunsford, a survivor of the Fort Hood shooting, told the BBC that the death penalty by firing squad is an appropriate punishment for the gunman. He said the sentence “befits the crime” and expressed support for that method of execution.

Lunsford also voiced reservations about allowing the execution to be broadcast, questioning whether the public should be able to watch the event.
summary: Alonzo Lunsford, a Fort Hood survivor, says the punishment befits the crime. He says he has some doubts whether the public should be able to watch it.
author: BBC World

title: Olivia Colman says viral Wicker memes are unprecedented for her
content:
Olivia Colman has commented on the surge of viral Wicker memes that have taken social media by storm. In an interview, she noted, “This has never happened to me before,” referring to the unexpected attention her name has received online.

The memes, which feature steamy jokes, have flooded platforms ahead of the release of Colman’s latest film. The actress has not yet addressed the specific content of the jokes, but the trend has generated significant online buzz surrounding her upcoming project.
summary: Olivia Colman said the viral Wicker memes were something she had never experienced before. Steamy jokes about the memes have flooded social media ahead of her latest film's release.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: South Africa vs Australia: First Men's Test Day One Live Coverage
content:
South Africa and Australia opened their first Test in Durban on 9 30 am local time (6 30 pm AEDT). The match, streamed live from Kingsmead Cricket Ground, pits the top two teams in the current World Test Championship standings against each other.

The fixture marks the first Test between the sides since the 2023 WTC final at Lord’s, where the Proteas defeated the defending champions Australia to claim a rare piece of silverware and shed a “choker” tag.

The series’ buildup also recalls the 2015 incident at Newlands when Cameron Bancroft exposed fractures in Australian cricket. The fallout saw the young opener, David Warner, and captain Steve Smith banned from playing for up to 12 months, triggering a prolonged culture reckoning within the national team.
summary: The first Test between South Africa and Australia began at 9:30 am local time (6:30 pm AEDT) at Kingsmead Cricket Ground in Durban. The match pits the top two teams in the World Test Championship standings, following South Africa's win over Australia in the previous cycle's final at Lord's.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pulis says Man City players can show unity on Anfield trip
content:
Tony Pulis, a columnist for BBC Sport, said that Manchester City players will have a good opportunity to display unity and togetherness when they travel to Anfield on Sunday.  

According to Pulis, Maresca will be demanding a siege mentality from the City side.
summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis says Manchester City players have a great chance to show unity and togetherness on their trip to Anfield. He believes the team can demonstrate solidarity during the match on Sunday.
author: BBC Sport

title: England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Republic of Ireland eye Women's World Cup play‑offs
content:
England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland are among the national teams hoping to qualify for next year's Women's World Cup.  

The teams will need to progress through the qualification play‑offs to secure a place in the tournament.

content:
Republican Senator Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson engaged in a contentious exchange during the second of two Senate debates held this week. The hourlong event, hosted by WMTW on Thursday, featured the candidates sparring over the Iran war and high prices as the race in Maine approaches Election Day.

During the debate, the rivals defended their respective political records and revisited many of the same issues raised in their previous encounter. The tone of the discussion turned testy at times, reflecting the intensity of the battleground contest.
summary: Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson squared off Thursday in the second Maine Senate debate of the week, sparring over the Iran war and high prices. The hourlong debate, hosted by WMTW, turned testy at times as the rivals defended their records and re-upped many.

content:
Arlington County has filed a lawsuit to block President Trump’s proposed triumphal arch after the project received approval from the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts in April.  

The county’s suit opposes construction of the proposed 250‑foot arch, citing concerns that the structure would negatively impact tourism and pose safety risks to local residents.  

“Using the Arch to store large…”
summary: Arlington County has filed a lawsuit to block President Trump’s proposed triumphal arch following the project’s approval by the U. S.

title: Chris Mason Faces Pressure Over Response to Zionism Racism Motion and By-Election Loss
content:
Green Party leader Chris Mason is facing his most significant leadership crisis to date, driven by internal pressure over his response to a party motion. The motion in question declared Zionism a form of racism, a stance that has generated substantial scrutiny for Mason.

This challenge comes alongside a recent by-election loss, which has further compounded the difficulties for the Green leader as he navigates these concurrent political pressures.
summary: Chris Mason is under pressure for his response to a party motion that declares Zionism a form of racism. He also lost a recent by-election.
author: BBC Politics

title: Africa Energy Bank launch delayed again, undermining oil and gas investment hopes
content:
The launch of the Africa Energy Bank has been delayed again, a setback that dampens expectations for new financing of Africa’s oil and gas sector.  

Repeated delays are raising questions about the bank’s momentum and whether it can mobilise investment to support the continent’s oil and gas ambitions amid the broader energy transition.  

The story first appeared on Climate Home News.
summary: Repeated delays of the Africa Energy Bank raise doubts about its ability to mobilise investment for Africa's oil and gas ambitions. The bank's momentum is questioned amid the energy transition era.
author: Climate Home News

title: Tories overstate net zero cost by nearly £500bn in apparent spreadsheet error
content:
Tories overstate net zero cost by nearly £500bn in apparent spreadsheet error

Kemi Badenoch’s flagship policy document for the Conservative conference in Birmingham, titled The Right Way, cites a net‑zero cost estimate of £957 billion—roughly twice the total reported by climate advisers. The figure appears to have been inflated by nearly £500 billion, likely due to an accidental double‑counting error in a spreadsheet.

The error is located in a chapter on net zero within the 100‑page document. Badenoch repeatedly referenced the £957 billion figure during her main conference speech, drawing attention to the discrepancy.

The document was produced for the party’s conference in Birmingham.
summary: Kemi Badenoch’s flagship conference policy document, The Right Way, cites a £957bn estimate for net zero, which is nearly £500bn higher than the total reported by climate advisers’ data. The overestimation appears to be due to a spreadsheet error that double‑counted figures, and Badenoch repeatedly used the phrase in her main speech at the Conservative conference in Birmingham.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Digital health promises shape the work of health care professionals
content:
Digital health promises shape the work of health care professionals

A recent study from the University of Eastern Finland shows that the future benefits expected from remote monitoring in health care are shaped by how professionals understand their current work and its associated challenges. The research indicates that professionals’ perceptions of their day‑to‑day tasks and the obstacles they face will determine how effectively remote monitoring technologies can be integrated into clinical practice.
summary: The future benefits expected from remote monitoring in health care are shaped by how professionals understand their current work and its associated challenges, a recent study from the University of Eastern Finland shows.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Family members become main victims in homicides linked to mental disorders
content:
Hidden violence: Family members as the main victims of homicides linked to mental disorders

The article notes that in recent decades the social and legal perception of people with mental disorders who commit crimes has changed. Initially, these individuals were considered dangerous. Since the late 20th century, the paradigm has shifted at both social and legal levels, with people experiencing mental disorders often considered victims themselves, despite having committed intentional crimes.

The title highlights that family members are the main victims of homicides linked to mental disorders.
summary: Family members are the primary victims in homicides involving people with mental disorders. Since the late 20th century, people with mental disorders have been increasingly viewed as victims rather than dangerous offenders, despite having committed intentional crimes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Social media offers valued community spaces for autistic young people
content:
Social media provides valued community spaces for autistic young people

Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition that influences how people communicate and process information. A significant proportion of autistic children do not speak or speak only a few words. Many find it difficult to communicate face to face, especially when interaction is fast‑moving or dependent on interpreting bodily cues.
summary: Social media offers valued community spaces for autistic young people. These platforms help children who struggle with face‑to‑face communication and limited speech to connect and share.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Researchers find circadian rhythms linked to blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes
content:
Daily rhythms may matter for blood sugar management in type 2 diabetes

A research team led by Dr. Lee Da young announced findings indicating that circadian rhythms (biorhythms) are closely related to blood glucose control in patients with type 2 diabetes. The team includes Dr. Nan Hee Kim of the Division of Endocrinology and Metabolism (Department of Internal Medicine, Ansan Hospital), Dr. Lee Heon-jeong of the Department of Psychiatry (Anam Hospital), and Dr. Lee Jung-been of the Division of Computer Science and Engineering (Sun Moon University). The study highlights a potential link between daily biological cycles and the regulation of blood sugar levels.
summary: A research team led by Dr. Lee Da young, Dr. Nan Hee Kim, Dr. Lee Heon-jeong and Dr. Lee Jung-been announced findings on type 2 diabetes. They indicated that circadian rhythms are closely related to blood glucose control in patients with the condition.
author: Medical Xpress

title: 3D printing-inspired tech introduced in hospitals to create personalized medicines
content:
Technology inspired by 3D printing is being introduced in hospitals and specialized pharmacies to produce personalized medicines tailored to individual patients.  

Mahsa Bahman’s doctoral thesis at Åbo Akademi University examined how this approach can improve dosing accuracy and expand the availability of customized treatments.  

The research highlights the potential for the technology to enhance precision in medication delivery and make individualized therapy more accessible in clinical settings.
summary: Technology inspired by 3D printing is being introduced in hospitals and specialized pharmacies to produce personalized medicines for individual patients. Mahsa Bahman's doctoral thesis at Åbo Akademi University examined how the approach could improve dosing accuracy and expand availability of customized treatments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Video games used in MRI scanners to map predictive and adaptive brain activity
content:
Video‑game tasks are being introduced inside MRI scanners to map how brains predict and adapt, researchers say.  

For decades, neuroscientists have studied the human brain by asking people to lie very still inside a brain scanner and perform carefully controlled tasks. Those experiments have revealed a remarkable amount about how the brain works.  

However, that approach “leaves out something fundamental,” prompting scientists to explore interactive video‑game paradigms that can capture dynamic brain activity while participants predict and adjust to changing gameplay.
summary: Neuroscientists have traditionally studied the brain by having participants lie still in scanners performing controlled tasks. New approaches now use video games inside MRI scanners to map how the brain predicts and adapts.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Patients' favorite music eases pain during IV cannula insertion before MRI
content:
A study examined whether music could ease the discomfort of an intravenous cannula insertion performed before magnetic resonance imaging. Researchers compared three musical conditions: classical pieces by Mozart, generic relaxation music, and each patient’s personally chosen favorite songs.

Participants who listened to their own favorite music reported the greatest reduction in pain and stress, outperforming those who heard Mozart or relaxation tracks. The findings suggest that selecting music that patients enjoy may be the most effective way to lessen the discomfort of minor medical procedures.
summary: Scientists compared Mozart, relaxation music, and patients' favorite tunes on people receiving an intravenous cannula insertion before an MRI. The study found that playing patients' favorite music worked best at reducing pain.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Longbow claims region uniquely suited for its car production
content:
Car maker Longbow asserts that its new vehicle can only be produced in a specific region, stating “you cannot build this car anywhere else in the world.” The company emphasizes that the area possesses the unique talent and know‑how required for the project.

Longbow, which aims to manufacture thousands of the cars, says the regional expertise makes it the sole viable location for production.
summary: Longbow hopes to build thousands of cars. The company says the region has the talent and know-how to build them and cannot be built elsewhere.
author: BBC Business

title: Study finds 1989 beef trade group knew cattle caused warming, chose PR focus
content:
A new study of a decade of industry records shows that a leading U.S. beef industry trade association was aware by 1989 that cattle contributed to global warming.  

Instead of addressing the emissions issue directly, the association focused its response on protecting consumer demand through public‑relations efforts.  

The research documents the group’s early strategy to counter climate concerns by emphasizing marketing rather than mitigation.
summary: The study shows a leading U.S. beef industry trade association was aware by 1989 that cattle contributed to global warming. Instead of addressing emissions, the association focused its response on protecting consumer demand through public‑relations efforts.

title: University of Alicante study links LGBT stories to inclusive attitudes in primary schools
content:
University of Alicante researchers investigate the impact of LGBT literature on elementary students

A study led by Guillermo Soler, María Ribes and José Rovira‑Collado from the Language and Literature Didactics area of the Department of Teaching Innovation and Training at the University of Alicante (UA) examines whether literature can foster greater acceptance of LGBT people among elementary school students. The researchers aim to explore the potential of LGBT stories to promote more inclusive attitudes in primary schools.
summary: Researchers Guillermo Soler, María Ribes and José Rovira‑Collado of the Language and Literature Didactics area in the Department of Teaching Innovation and Training at the University of Alicante conducted a study on this question. The study asks whether literature can foster greater acceptance of LGBT people among elementary school students.

title: Study finds most trading card packs conceal odds of rare cards
content:
Most trading card packs hide the odds of winning rare cards, study finds

A recent study highlights that Pokémon, sports, and other physical trading and collectible cards—long available for decades—have surged in popularity since the COVID‑19 pandemic. The cards are typically obtained through gambling‑like packs that contain random cards.

Most packs do not include highly desirable cards, but a few do. Because of this, consumers—often including children—buy many packs in the hope of obtaining rare chase cards.
summary: A study reports that most physical trading‑card packs, including Pokémon and sports cards, do not disclose the odds of receiving rare chase cards. Since COVID, the popularity of these packs has surged, prompting consumers, often children, to buy many packs hoping to obtain a rare card.
author: Phys.org

title: Umeå University researchers study AI and mixed reality for police work
content:
Research shows how AI and mixed reality can enhance police work

Researchers at Umeå University are investigating how AI can support police officers in complex situations. The study is an interdisciplinary collaboration between the university’s police research and computing science departments. It examines both the opportunities and risks associated with using AI‑based interactive systems in police work.
summary: Researchers in police research and computing science at Umeå University examined how AI-based interactive systems could support police officers in complex situations. Their interdisciplinary work explores both opportunities and risks of using AI and mixed reality in policing.
author: Phys.org

title: Study Shows Armed Conflict Accelerates Cropland Loss, Effects Last Years
content:
A new study published in Nature Food on Sept. 24 finds that armed conflict speeds the loss of cropland worldwide.  

The research shows that the impact of conflict on farmland can continue for years after hostilities begin and that the degree of loss differs markedly depending on the severity of the fighting and the surrounding social conditions.  

These findings highlight how warfare can erode agricultural land and diminish potential food production over extended periods.
summary: A new study published in Nature Food on Sept. 24 found that armed conflict accelerates cropland loss. The study also reports that the effects can persist for years after conflict begins and vary with conflict severity and social conditions.
author: Phys.org

content:

summary: Scientists have produced a new statewide surface geologic map of Nebraska. title: Stanford PhD Student Samuel King Uses AI to Design Virus Blueprints
content:
Stanford University PhD student Samuel King used a generative AI model in 2025 to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses, prompting the question of whether AI can design new life forms. The work, described in a roundtable discussion announced on Friday, October 16, 2026, represents a preliminary step toward AI‑generated biology, though it is not yet an example of AI‑created life.

King’s approach involved leveraging the AI system to generate potential viral genomes, offering a proof‑of‑concept that machine learning can assist in designing biological entities. While the resulting blueprints remain theoretical, the research suggests that fully AI‑designed organisms could follow.

The roundtable, titled “A Conversation With the Creator of AI‑Designed Viruses,” will feature senior AI reporter participation to explore the implications of King’s work.
summary: In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. The work is not yet an example of AI-generated life but could be next.

title: Feds prepare to rewrite car headlight regulations
content:
Federal officials are preparing to rewrite regulations governing automobile headlights. The upcoming changes aim to address two primary objectives.

The revisions will focus on reducing glare from vehicle lighting while also permitting the use of modern light technologies in new car models.

content:

content:

content: SpaceX has urged improved coordination of orbital traffic after reporting near‑miss incidents involving its Starlink satellites. The company said the events resulted in conjunctions ranging from tens of meters to hundreds of meters, describing the distances as “way too close to comfort.”

title: Kyiv open to constructive dialogue with Seoul after ambassador recall amid POW row
content:
Kyiv says it remains open to “constructive dialogue” with Seoul despite the South Korean decision to recall its ambassador, a move linked to a dispute over North Korean prisoner‑of‑war disclosures.

The recall follows a statement made days earlier by South Korea’s president, who warned of punitive action against President Zelenskyy for violating a non‑disclosure agreement. The diplomatic tension stems from the row over the disclosure of North Korean POWs.
summary: Kyiv says it is open to “constructive dialogue” with Seoul despite Seoul’s decision to recall its ambassador. The recall came days after South Korea’s president warned of punitive action against Zelenskyy for breaching a non‑disclosure agreement.

title: Masked ICE officers shoot man during New York arrest, officials say
content:
Masked Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers shot a man while making an arrest in New York, officials said.

Eyewitnesses reported that a few masked officers wearing Department of Homeland Security‑branded clothing surrounded a man on the ground who appeared injured, and that they heard three or four gunshots being fired.
summary: Officials say masked ICE officers shot a man while making an arrest in New York. Eyewitnesses reported masked officers in Department of Homeland Security clothing surrounding an injured man and hearing three or four gunshots.

title: Six injured as heavy rains flood Chile's capital, sweep away cars
content:
Heavy rains battered Chile’s capital, sweeping away cars and flooding homes, leaving six people injured, officials said.  

In response, authorities placed ten additional Chilean districts on high alert because of the heightened risk of mudslides and other rain‑related emergencies threatening the region.
summary: Heavy rains battered Chile's capital, injuring six people, sweeping away cars and flooding homes. Authorities placed ten other Chilean districts on high alert because of potential mudslides and rain‑related emergencies.

title: Russia cuts federal cancer programme budget to 3.87 bn roubles as defence share hits 35%
content:
Russia has sharply cut funding for its federal cancer programme, reducing the budget from 44.9 billion roubles in 2025 to 3.87 billion roubles in 2027, a nearly 40‑fold decrease.

The cuts come as defence spending has risen to 35 % of all federal expenditure, the highest share since the Soviet Union collapsed.
summary: The federal cancer programme budget will drop from 44.9 billion to 3.87 billion roubles in 2027, a nearly 40‑fold reduction from 2025 levels. Defence spending will reach 35% of all federal expenditure, the highest share since the Soviet Union collapsed.

title: French students retake Bastille, Zelenskyy says US unwilling to help Ukraine
content:
French students declared they have “retaken the Bastille,” Jean‑Luc Mélenchon said after a mass rally in Paris.  

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the United States of “unwillingness” to help Ukraine.  

Former New Zealand prime minister Helen Clark joined a discussion on critical minerals, while MEP Rima Hassan faced fallout over a flags row.

title: US military to livestream Nidal Hasan's firing squad execution, first since WWII
content:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the execution of Nidal Hasan, the convicted shooter at Fort Hood, will be livestreamed.  

Hasan will be executed by firing squad, marking the first U.S. military execution by that method since World War II.  

The livestream will broadcast the execution.
summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the convicted shooter Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad. This will be the first US military firing squad execution since World War II.

title: USS Lincoln docks in California, ending 265‑day deployment amid reports of onboard issues
content:
The USS Lincoln docked in California on Thursday, ending a record deployment of 265 days of uninterrupted time at sea. The ship’s return marked the conclusion of a 10‑month deployment that had been extended by the war in Iran.

The deployment was described as troubled, with reports of deteriorating conditions onboard. Crew members were reunited with family they had not seen in nearly a year after the mission’s length was prolonged by the conflict.
summary: The USS Lincoln docked in California on Thursday, ending a record 265‑day deployment at sea. Crew members reunited with family they had not seen in nearly a year after the mission was prolonged by the war in Iran.
author: France 24

title: Flavio Bolsonaro gains endorsement from third‑place candidate Augusto Cury
content:
Brazil’s right‑wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro secured the endorsement of third‑place finisher Augusto Cury on Thursday, bolstering his campaign against incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ahead of the runoff.

Cury, who captured nearly three percent of the vote in Sunday’s first round, joined Bolsonaro’s effort as the contest narrows. A Datafolha poll released after the endorsement shows Bolsonaro leading with 52 percent to Lula’s 48 percent.
summary: Flavio Bolsonaro secured the endorsement of Augusto Cury, who finished third in Brazil’s first‑round presidential vote with nearly three percent. A Datafolha poll shows Bolsonaro ahead of incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, 52% to 48%, ahead of the runoff.

title: Morocco and Senegal await CAS verdict on AFCON title after hearing
content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) held a long‑awaited hearing in Lausanne on Thursday to consider Senegal’s appeal over the decision to award Morocco the Africa Cup of Nations title.

Senegal had won the match on the pitch in Rabat ten months ago, but the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned the result after the Teranga Lions left the pitch in protest mid‑game before returning. The CAF decision has led to the current arbitration case.

A three‑judge panel will issue a verdict soon, concluding the dispute over the tournament’s championship.
summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport held a hearing in Lausanne on Senegal's appeal against the decision to award Morocco this year's Africa Cup of Nations title. The Confederation of African Football had overturned Senegal's on‑field win in Rabat after the team left the pitch in protest, and the three‑judge panel will issue its verdict soon.
author: France 24

title: New giant waterlily species discovered in Colombian jungle, visible from space
content:
A new species of giant waterlily was discovered in the depths of Colombia’s jungle after a plant selfie captured on social media. The photo sparked a race‑against‑time effort to identify the plant, which had remained hidden in the remote jungle until now.

The species is notable for its enormous leaves, large enough to be seen from space. It is already classified as critically endangered, and plans are afoot to protect it.

The discovery came about through a chance social media encounter, highlighting the role of online platforms in accelerating scientific findings.
summary: A chance social‑media encounter led researchers to discover a new giant waterlily species hidden in Colombia’s jungle. The plant’s leaves are large enough to be seen from space, it is already classified as critically endangered, and plans are afoot to protect it.
author: Guardian World

title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest after six colleagues charged with terrorism
content:
Egyptian journalists from the independent fact‑checking and investigative platform Matsadaash are set to stage a protest in Cairo this weekend after six of their colleagues were detained on terrorism charges. The authorities arrested the journalists last week, accusing them of operating without a license and publishing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.

Matsadaash staff allege that the detained journalists were subjected to torture and forced to give confessions while in police custody. The planned demonstration is intended to draw attention to the charges and the reported mistreatment.
summary: Egyptian journalists from the independent fact‑checking platform Matsadaash are planning a protest in Cairo this weekend after six of their colleagues were arrested. The six journalists were charged with terrorism offences and the platform alleges they were tortured in police detention after being accused of working for the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.
author: Guardian World

title: Christa Pike case highlights frequent botched lethal injections in US
content:
The case of Christa Pike has drawn attention to the frequency of botched executions in the United States, according to the article’s headline.  

Experts note that while lethal injection is promoted as a more humane method of carrying out the death penalty, it is often plagued by mishaps.  

These observations highlight ongoing concerns about the reliability of execution protocols.
summary: The Christa Pike case underscores the prevalence of botched executions in the United States. Experts say lethal injection, promoted as a humane method, is often marred by mishaps.

title: ICE shooting of New York man with 5-year-old in car draws mayor, governor condemnation
content:
ICE agents shot a New York man who was in a car with his 5‑year‑old child, an incident that has ignited protests across the city.

The city’s mayor, the state governor, and several U.S. lawmakers publicly condemned the shooting by Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Demonstrators gathered in response to the incident, calling for accountability and an end to such actions.
summary: ICE agents shot a New York man who was in a car with his 5-year-old child. The mayor, governor and U.S. lawmakers condemned the shooting as protests erupted in the city.

title: Sinn Fein faces police probe as DUP urges prosecution of its lawmakers
content:
Northern Ireland’s Sinn Fein is under a police investigation following a protest that has heightened tensions in the region, according to the article’s headline.  

The Democratic Unionist Party has publicly called for the prosecution of Sinn Fein lawmakers who took part in the demonstration.  

The call for legal action underscores the growing political dispute surrounding the protest.

content:

content:

title: Abdominal fluid reveals rare immune cells that may limit attacks on tumors
content: A study published in Science Immunology utilized malignant ascites, a fluid that accumulates in the abdomen when cancer metastasizes to the abdominal cavity, to identify immune programs associated with metastatic disease. The research team discovered a rare population of RORC-expressing dendritic cells within this fluid, a cell type not previously linked to human cancer.
summary: Researchers used malignant ascites from patients with metastatic cancer to uncover immune programs associated with the disease. The study identified a rare population of RORC-expressing dendritic cells that had not previously been linked to human cancer.

title: Peanut consumption linked to changes in circulating blood lipid profile
content:
Unhealthy dietary patterns are identified as a primary driver of the global health crisis, contributing significantly to increased rates of obesity, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Nutritional science emphasizes that the quality of dietary fat is essential for metabolic health, with evidence showing that reducing saturated fat intake or substituting it with unsaturated fats lowers the risk of CVD and T2D. These dietary changes improve blood lipid profiles and reduce inflammation.

While traditional blood lipid profiles concentrate on key markers such as cholesterol, advanced lipidomics offers a comprehensive perspective on the entire circulating lipidome. This approach reveals specific alterations in lipid classes, providing a more detailed understanding of how dietary factors like peanut consumption affect the lipid profile in the blood.
summary: Unhealthy dietary patterns significantly contribute to rising rates of obesity, cardiovascular disease, and type 2 diabetes. Advanced lipidomics provides a comprehensive view of the entire circulating lipidome, uncovering specific changes in lipid classes.

title: UCL Study Finds 'Immune Fog' May Flag Lung Cancer Risk Years Before Tumor Develops
content:
Researchers at University College London (UCL) have identified a "rising fog" that may cloud the immune system's ability to detect tumors, potentially serving as an early indicator of lung cancer years before a formal diagnosis. This "immune fog" appears to be a key factor in the development of the disease.

The UCL team tracked this specific signal by utilizing prototype blood tests. Additionally, the researchers successfully reversed the fog using drugs, suggesting a potential pathway for early intervention in lung cancer.
summary: A research team at University College London identified a 'rising fog' that clouds the immune system's ability to detect developing tumors. The team used prototype blood tests to follow this signal and successfully reversed it using drugs.

title: St. Jude scientists identify neuroblastoma gene signature linked to poor prognosis
content:
Neuroblastoma, the most common solid tumor found outside the brain in children, presents a clinical challenge due to the poorly understood reasons why some patients respond well to treatment while others do not. To address this, scientists from St. Jude Children's Research Hospital and their collaborators developed one of the most comprehensive datasets of neuroblastoma cells to date.

Using this dataset, the research team defined the tumor's various cell types and identified a specific gene signature. This signature marks a malignant cell population that is associated with poor prognosis in neuroblastoma patients.
summary: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital scientists and collaborators built a comprehensive dataset to define neuroblastoma cell types. The study identified a gene signature marking a malignant cell population associated with poor patient outcomes.

summary: Tampere University Hospital has begun offering a new radiotherapy that targets high doses of radiation at the tumor surface to destroy rectal cancer. This treatment aims to allow more patients to avoid major surgery and a potentially permanent stoma.

content:

The study involved an analysis of 22 experimental investigations focusing on the impact of specific air pollutants, namely ozone and nitrogen oxides (NOx), on pollinator behavior.

The findings show that both ozone and nitrogen oxides impair the ability of pollinators to locate flowers by breaking down or altering the chemical scents emitted by the plants. This chemical interference makes it more difficult for these insects to identify and navigate to their food sources.

title: Pocketty: iPhone SSH terminal with encrypted push alerts for blocked agents
content:
Pocketty is a new SSH terminal application for iPhone and iPad, developed by the creator of herdr, a tool that manages agent panes on a user’s computer. The app was created to allow the developer to remain productive during paternity leave without being tied to a desk, enabling the use of nap breaks for work tasks. Pocketty connects directly to a computer via plain SSH, with Tailscale suggested as a simple method for remote access, though any reachable SSH host is supported.

The application features a small Rust daemon on the host that monitors herdr’s state. When an agent requires attention, the daemon encrypts an alert using HPKE (X25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305) with the phone’s key. These sealed bytes are sent to Apple Push Notification servers through a stateless relay on Cloudflare Workers, which cannot read the data or retain it. The SSH key is generated in the Secure Enclave and is non-exportable.

For the terminal interface, Pocketty uses libghostty-vt for state management and wgpu on Metal for rendering, allowing full-screen TUIs to display correctly on the mobile device. The app includes features such as diffs for agent turns, a file browser, and previews of localhost dev servers, all accessed through the same SSH connection without port forwarding. Herdr and the daemon are optional, allowing the app to function as a standard SSH client.

Pocketty operates without accounts, analytics, or tracking. It offers a 14-day free trial with full feature access, followed by a one-time purchase price of $99 for the first two weeks of launch, increasing to $129 thereafter.
summary: Pocketty is an SSH terminal for iPhone and iPad that uses a Rust daemon and Cloudflare relay to send encrypted notifications when an agent needs attention. The app offers a 14-day free trial followed by a one-time purchase price of $99 during a launch promotion.

content:

content:

The acquisition includes up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, which SpaceX says will allow Starlink Mobile’s signal to penetrate through walls and buildings.

Upon Federal Communications Commission approval, SpaceX plans to deploy a new architecture that combines its satellite-to-mobile constellation with a terrestrial mobile network. This infrastructure is designed to compete directly with existing carriers T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.

content:

Open‑source projects that opt in will receive “thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost.” The scans are fully model‑generated, with no human review or triage. While this approach enables faster and more frequent scanning, the reports may contain incorrect or invalid findings.

The full story is reported by The Verge.
summary: Anthropic has introduced OSS Scanner, a service that provides free, periodic security scans for opt-in open-source projects. The reports are fully model-generated without human review, which allows for faster scanning but may result in incorrect or invalid findings.

content: Researchers have achieved a significant experimental milestone by entangling a glass bead with light, effectively enabling the bead to behave as a quantum object.
